messages.body_plain:

I have a large set of Gal4 expression pattern for larval zebrafish and I would like to convert them to dotprops so I can search for lines that have a specific neuron type using NBLAST. I already thresholded the image, skeletonized it and saved it as nrrd. How do I now convert the .nnrd file into a dotprop object?

Best,
Michael

messages.subject: Re: [nat-user] generate dps files for Gal4 images
messages.subject_clean: [nat-user] generate dps files for Gal4 images
messages.body_plain:
Dear Michael,

> I have a large set of Gal4 expression pattern for larval zebrafish and I would like to convert them to dotprops so I can search for lines that have a specific neuron type using NBLAST. I already thresholded the image, skeletonized it and saved it as nrrd. How do I now convert the .nnrd file into a dotprop object?

That’s great. I’ll be very interested to hear how the search works. You’ve done the difficult part. Here is some sample code:

ff = dir(pattern = "nrrd$")

# it's a good id to set this to some kind of ifentifier for each line
names(ff) <- tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(ff))

# choice of k may depend somewhat on spatial scale of branches etc in
# your expression patterns
gal4s=nlapply(ff[1:3], dotprops, k=5)

# you can add additional metadata to the neuronlist object like so
gal4s[,'id']=names(gal4s)
gal4s[,]=merge(gal4s[,], metadata_table)

To find out more about neuronlist objects (the wrapper for multiple neurons or expression patterns), see http://jefferis.github.io/nat/articles/neurons-intro.html.

Best wishes,

Greg.

messages.subject: How do you generate a neuron object based on the flycircuit identifier?
messages.subject_clean: How do you generate a neuron object based on the flycircuit identifier?
messages.body_plain:
Hello,
I've been using the flycircuit package to plot flycircuit clones, but I haven't been able to figure out how to convert these into neuron objects that I can manipulate using the nat package. Is there a way to do this?
Thanks!

messages.subject: Re: [nat-user] How do you generate a neuron object based on the flycircuit identifier?
messages.subject_clean: [nat-user] How do you generate a neuron object based on the flycircuit identifier?
messages.body_plain:
Dear Isabel,

Thanks for your interest. The neurons distributed with the flycircuit package are in dotprops format - basically they are broken into short segments. See http://jefferis.github.io/nat/reference/dotprops.html

Right now the easiest way to get a full traced neuron is just to download straight from the flycircuit website. There is a convenience function for this in an experimental package developed by a student in our group, Alex Bates:

http://jefferislab.github.io/catnat/reference/get.skeleton.from.flycircuit.html

Note that this uses the FlyCircuit’s group own registration approach, which is different from our 2016 NBLAST paper.

Let me know if you have further questions.

Best wishes,

Greg.

Sent from my iPhone

messages.subject: Re: using NBLAST online to compare neurons in the zebrafish brain
messages.subject_clean: using NBLAST online to compare neurons in the zebrafish brain
messages.body_plain:
Dear Abhi,

The current online version of NBLAST does not have any zebrafish neurons
in the associated dataset.

You can definitely use the NBLAST approach to compare your traced
zebrafish neurons amongst themselves – we gave a small example of this
in the original NBLAST paper, but right now we do not have an online
tool to compare a set of neurons, with each other. This still has to be
done with the command line tools we have written.

See
http://flybrain.mrc-lmb.cam.ac.uk/si/nblast/www/nblast_desktop/#kenyon-cells-example
for a basic example. The main things you will need to do:

1. Read in your neurons see
http://jefferis.github.io/nat/reference/read.neurons.html
2. Decide on a scaling factor to make fish neurons about the same size
as fly neurons (this simplifies things)
3. Mirror your neurons across the midline if you want to compare
irrespective of brain hemisphere.

You can see a full example for zebrafish mitral cells from our original
NBLAST paper here:

https://github.com/jefferislab/Cross_Species_Examples/blob/master/Mitral.Rmd

Best wishes,

Greg.

PS I have taken the liberty of ccing this message to the nat-user google
group since the answer may be of interest to others.

messages.subject: Adding a template brain
messages.body_plain:
Hi Greg,

I've been using nat and nat.nblast for comparison of traced zebrafish neurons, and once I figured out how to import the .swc files and dataframes it's been working great-- thank you for this resource!
I was wondering if there is a way to add a template brain to the 3D plot of neurons. We already have a registered fish brain, we just want to be able to superimpose the neurons, which are now different colors based on their proximity in the dendrogram, onto our registered brain. Is there a way to do this using your packages?

Thank you!
LauraAnn

messages.subject: Re: [nat-user] Adding a template brain
messages.body_plain:
Dear Laura, thanks for your message and interest in nat. It’s great to hear that it’s proving useful for fish neurons.

You can read in a surface mesh representation of your template brain for 3d plots. nat has built in support for Amira surfaces. You can use the readobj package to read in wavefront obj format surfaces (a very standard format) - make sure to choose the rgl mesh3d as your return type. You can the plot the surface with rgl functions like shade3d or wire3d.

Best,

Greg.

Sent from my iPhone
